stage1.impression: This is a coherent system. The globe is built from six flat discs: a green ball, three latitude bands and two crossed meridians. There are six different arrivals and one shared ending: the upright globe leans to an axial tilt, holds a beat, then shrinks and slides left while a heavy black EARF is wiped in beside it, and the end card holds still for about 1.4 s. On paper the six-colour palette is warm and balanced, and the lockup is centred and confident. The good ideas are the ones that use the discs. In Open, five edge-on strokes swing open into the globe; its first frame is the best single frame in the set. In Coin, one disc flips through every colour and then turns into the globe. But Coin, the lead ident, spends its first 2 s of 5.25 s on six identical flips of one flat disc. The trace never settles, nothing builds or accumulates, and it reads as a blinking dot until the globe lands. Every variant then stops dead for roughly half a second (the flat stretch after the tilt) and restarts into a generic shrink, slide and wipe. The lean is the one move that could only be Earth, yet it is the smallest bump on every trace. Open's ball snaps open in two frames. Gyro starts cold, already mid-spin. Rise's horizon is an invisible cut in the middle of the frame. Roll and Download are arrivals any round logo could use, and Download's square of pixels fights the disc language. On night, the see-through discs dull every colour by about a fifth and mix olive and teal, so the mark looks muddier on screen than on paper. The mark is drawable in outline but busy at lockup size, and nothing here shows it in one colour. It is better than a draft in idea and system, but not yet fluid, and there are too many variants.

keep: Open's arrival (sheet 5, frames 01-04). The flat globe icon, five edge-on strokes, turns disc by disc into the 3D globe in under 0.9 s. It is the most minimal opener, it is built from the mark's own construction, and its first frame would work as a one-colour sign.

Coin's colour-wheel run landing on the green ball (sheet 1, frames 01-08). One disc flashes yellow through green at 0.34 s per half turn, just inside three flashes a second, then turns onto the globe at the spin's own speed. It answers the owner's brief and shows how the mark is made.

changes.problem: Every ident stops dead for more than half a second between the lean and the move aside, so the motion dies and restarts like two clips cut together, which is exactly the owner's 'doesn't seem fluid or quick enough'.
changes.evidence: All seven traces share one flat stretch. Sheet 1 is under 0.2% from 2.60 to 3.13 s (0.567 s), and frames 10 and 11 (2.83 and 3.13 s) are identical. The same 0.567 s still appears on sheet 2 (2.60-3.13 s), sheet 3 (1.00-1.53 s), sheet 4 (1.13-1.67 s), sheet 5 (0.87-1.40 s), sheet 6 (1.10-1.63 s) and sheet 7 (0.90-1.43 s). The tilt's lean-past-and-settle is already below 0.2% from 2.60 s, and HOLD then adds 0.35 s of nothing.
changes.expected: The lean settles, holds a beat of about a third of a second, and glides aside as one gesture instead of stop-start. The tilted globe still registers at rest before it moves. Every ident gets 0.25 s shorter: Coin becomes about 4.9 s with change 2, and Open about 3.1 s with changes 3-5. Run this test on the Coin sheet.

changes.problem: The coin's landing slows to a full stop before the tilt starts, so it still reads as a separate animation between the spin and the tilt, which is the owner's round-24b note.
changes.evidence: Sheet 1 trace: the landing decays from 0.0265 at 2.07 s to 0.0014 at 2.30 s. Then nothing moves (under 0.2%) from 2.30 to 2.40 s, 0.133 s (on sheet 2, 2.27-2.40 s, 0.167 s), and only then does the tilt begin. Frame 07 (2.17 s) shows the globe at 80% width mid-landing; frame 08 (2.40 s) shows the same globe parked upright before anything leans.
changes.expected: The tilt starts at 2.30 s, the moment the landing's last visible movement dies. The globe is at 98% of its width then, so it still reads as whole and upright as it lands. Spin, landing and lean become one throw-and-settle with no parked frames, and everything after moves 0.1 s earlier.

changes.problem: In Open, the green ball snaps from a line to most of a disc in about two frames, the one jump among the arrivals worth keeping, so the unfolding reads as a pop.
changes.evidence: Sheet 5 trace: a sharp spike at 0.20-0.23 s (0.0185, then 0.0233), up from 0.0069 at 0.17 s and back down to 0.0129 at 0.27 s. Between frame 01 (0.00 s, the flat icon) and frame 02 (0.23 s), the ball is already a fat ellipse while every other disc is still a line.
changes.expected: Each disc opens over 0.6 s, so the ball takes about six frames rather than four to reach 90% open, and its fastest frame moves about a third less. The spike becomes a rounded hump. With change 4, the arrival ends at 0.92 s instead of 0.87 s.

changes.problem: The six discs open as a drawn-out six-step cascade, so a parallel is still lying as a flat bar across the finished ball; it looks like a stick laid on the globe, not minimal.
changes.evidence: Sheet 5 frame 03 (0.47 s): the ball and meridians are open, but the south parallel is still a yellow bar drawn whole in front across the bottom of the ball. The disc starts run from 0.12 to 0.47 s.
changes.expected: The discs open as one bloom, with the first and last starts 0.20 s apart instead of 0.35 s. With change 3, both parallels turn into their slotted lenses by about 0.39 s, before the ball finishes opening at about 0.49 s, so no frame shows a bar on a finished globe.

accept.check: Is every parallel already its slotted lens by the time the ball is fully open, with no flat bar lying across the finished ball?

changes.problem: Open's arrival also parks before its tilt, a smaller copy of the coin's hitch.
changes.evidence: Sheet 5 trace: under 0.2% from 0.53 to 0.67 s (0.167 s), between the last disc opening (0.0036 at 0.50 s) and the tilt starting at 0.67 s. Frame 04 (0.70 s) shows the globe still essentially upright.
changes.expected: With changes 3-4, the bloom's visible motion ends near 0.49 s, and the tilt now starts at 0.52 s (0.92 - 0.4). The globe opens and leans in one movement while the parallels finish their last, invisible stretch of opening.

changes.problem: The coin barely reads as a coin: its rim is half a real coin's thickness, so at each edge-on moment it thins to a hairline, like a card turning rather than a coin spinning on its edge.
changes.evidence: The card sets COIN.thick at 0.07 of the radius; real coins are about 0.14-0.24 of their radius thick. The coin on sheet 1 is 153 px across, so at each edge-on moment (0.34, 0.68 ... 2.04 s) the rim is about 5 px. Frames 01-06 are picked at the faces, so the storyboard never shows it.
changes.expected: At each edge-on moment the coin shows as a solid bar about 11 px wide in the face's colour. The spin then reads as a thick coin turning on its edge, which is the owner's 'looks like a coin spinning', and the silhouette never thins to a hairline. Add one edge-on frame (0.68 s) to the Coin sheet.

accept.check: Edge on, does the coin show as a solid bar about a seventh of its radius wide rather than a hairline?

most_important: Set HOLD from 0.35 to 0.1. All seven runs stall for 0.567 s between the lean and the glide aside. That stall is the main reason none of them feels fluid or quick, and one shared number fixes it across the whole set.
out_of_scope: The coin can't be made quick or minimal while all six colours must flash first at under three flashes a second. Together those fix about 2 s of one flat disc flickering at 2.9 Hz before any globe appears (sheet 1, 0-2.04 s, a trace that never settles), and COIN.half at 0.34 is already the floor. Coin will stay the longest and busiest ident, about 4.9 s even after these changes. The owner's 'quick' and 'all colours first' pull against each other.

Acrylic on ink: the see-through discs, at about 78% opacity, darken every colour by about a fifth (yellow is #E9B320 on paper and #B98F25 on ink) and mix olive and teal where they overlap (sheet 2, frames 08 and 16). The mark is therefore muddier on ink than on paper. Styles and grounds are fixed, but this matters because screens and video are where the ident plays.

At lockup size (82 px, sheet 1 frame 16), the tilted globe shows about twenty facets plus slivers at the rim. Geometry and colours are fixed, so there is a limit to how small the full-colour mark can go, and the lines style has to carry small sizes. That one-colour style hasn't been shown in motion yet.

The hand-off itself (shrink, slide left, wipe the name in) is about the most common lockup move there is. Its structure is fixed, so only its timing is tuned here, and it is the main reason the endings could belong to any brand.
for_owner: Which idents to keep. We recommend Coin as the long form, for films, and Open as the short form, for the site, with Roll as an optional third: its arrival eases down evenly into the lean without a stop (sheet 6). Retire Gyroscope: you already called it chaotic, it opens cold mid-spin, and it parks twice (0.57-0.80 s and 1.00-1.53 s). Retire Earthrise: its horizon is an invisible cut in the middle of the frame (sheet 4, frames 02-03), and it is the slowest arrival. Retire Download: it opens on a frozen square of blocks for 0.2 s, and a square of pixels contradicts the discs. Six arrivals onto one ending dilute the signature, so we'd rather polish these than add a seventh.

Whether the globe may count as the coin's sixth face, since its ball is green. The run would flash yellow through blue and then land on the globe, saving 0.34 s and avoiding the green coin followed by the green ball (frames 06-08). It bends 'flash between all colors first', so it's your call.
Whether acrylic is used on ink at all. Discs on ink would keep the colours at full strength.
Site delivery: at 30 fps the coin turns 17.6 degrees a frame, so each edge-on moment passes in about three frames. A 60 fps or real-time version for the site would look noticeably smoother.
